request_context: A request to split a project's user stories and high-level design into separate work streams that individual engineers can build largely independently.

rules.source_quote: this phrasing means produce the Feature Split format below, NOT a generic layer-by-layer technical breakdown
rules.outcome: The answer divides the work into vertical, self-contained features, each owned by one engineer, rather than horizontal technical layers such as data model, backend, API and frontend.
rules.why: A layer-by-layer breakdown forces engineers to wait on each other and defeats the goal of independent tracks.
rules.scenario_hint: User asks to break a feature or project down into implementation tasks.

rules.source_quote: Be independently implementable** — one engineer can complete it without blocking on others
rules.outcome: Each proposed feature can be completed by a single engineer without waiting for another feature to be finished first.
rules.why: Features that block each other serialize the team and cause idle time.
rules.scenario_hint: Splitting a design where some parts naturally build on others.

rules.outcome: No two or more features depend on each other in a cycle; any such cycle is removed by merging features or extracting a shared interface.
rules.why: Circular dependencies make it impossible to start or finish the work in any order.
rules.scenario_hint: Design where two components call each other's functionality.

rules.source_quote: User stories are missing from the split (every story must map to a feature)
rules.outcome: Every user story supplied is assigned to at least one feature, and each feature names the stories it serves, so nothing is left uncovered.
rules.why: Unmapped stories are silently dropped from implementation.
rules.scenario_hint: A set of many user stories, some of which are cross-cutting or easy to overlook.

rules.source_quote: Have clear boundaries** — well-defined inputs, outputs, and interfaces
rules.outcome: Each feature states its scope and its inputs, outputs and the interfaces it exposes or consumes, so its boundary is unambiguous.
rules.why: Vague boundaries lead to overlapping work and integration surprises.
rules.scenario_hint: Splitting a design with several services and endpoints.

rules.source_quote: if two features touch the same data model or API, consider merging or defining a shared interface
rules.outcome: Where several features rely on a common entity or endpoint, the answer either merges them or identifies a common contract to be defined up front and says which features use it.
rules.why: Uncoordinated changes to shared data or endpoints cause conflicts and rework.
rules.scenario_hint: Design in which several features read and write the same entity.

rules.source_quote: More than 2 features share the same data model (consider a shared-interfaces feature)
rules.outcome: When more than two features share one data model, the answer proposes a dedicated foundational piece of work that defines it first instead of letting each feature change it.
rules.why: Many features editing one model concurrently creates contention and inconsistent changes.
rules.scenario_hint: Three or more features all depend on one core entity such as a user or order.

rules.source_quote: A feature is too large (>2 weeks of work for one engineer)
rules.outcome: No feature is sized beyond roughly a fortnight of effort for a single person, and very small pieces of a few days or less are combined with related ones.
rules.why: Oversized features cannot be owned by one person and tiny ones add coordination overhead.
rules.scenario_hint: Design containing one very large area and several trivial ones.

rules.source_quote: Be testable in isolation** — can be verified without other features being complete
rules.outcome: Each feature can be verified on its own, without needing other features to be finished.
rules.why: Features that can only be tested together hide defects until late integration.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to split a project into engineer-sized features.

rules.outcome: The answer presents the split as a proposal and invites the user to confirm or adjust it before further work proceeds.
rules.why: Committing the team to an unreviewed split risks wasted effort.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to split a project into engineer-sized features.

rules.source_quote: Could suggest implementation order based on dependencies
rules.outcome: The answer suggests an order or effort estimate for the features, based on their dependencies, noting which interfaces must be defined first.
rules.why: Without ordering guidance, engineers may start work that depends on undefined interfaces.
rules.scenario_hint: Split where some features rely on shared interfaces.

rules.outcome: Each feature is presented as its own section listing scope, mapped stories, key components, dependencies and owner (or undecided), followed by a separate list of shared interfaces.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to split a project into engineer-sized features.
